dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To better understand what's happening, do your symptoms like the double vision or muscle weakness tend to get worse as the day goes on or after you've been active?

Yes, exactly! I notice that after I've been working at my computer for a while or doing any kind of physical activity, the double vision gets worse and my muscles feel much weaker. But if I take a break and rest for a few hours, I feel so much better - it's like the symptoms just fade away.
Just so you know, I'm an AI assistant and this call is recorded for quality. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids, or have you had any trouble swallowing or speaking clearly?

Now that you mention it, yes - sometimes my eyelids do feel heavy, especially later in the day when I'm tired. I haven't really had trouble swallowing, but occasionally my voice sounds a bit different or weaker when I've been talking for a long time.

I understand. Does the difficulty you experience when climbing stairs also improve significantly after you have rested, or is that weakness more constant? Also, have you had any shortness of breath lately?
Yes, the weakness in my legs when climbing stairs definitely gets better after I rest - it follows the same pattern as my other symptoms. And no, I haven't had any shortness of breath at all.
That pattern of fatigue is very specific. Have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your limbs, or is it strictly a loss of strength? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody_

RESULTS: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies - Present (elevated)

This is an abnormal finding. The presence of elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies is a significant positive result that supports the diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis, an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder.
